name: Namban Rengo
who: Tokyo's oldest international run club; free Wednesday interval sessions at Yoyogi Park's Oda Field, open to anyone.
why: Running since 1989, the template international crew that every later Tokyo club cites as the original.

name: AFE (Athletics Far East)
who: Tokyo running-lifestyle crew of creatives, models and designers; group runs plus its own apparel drops.
why: Modeled on 1970s club Athletics West, AFE turned Tokyo running into a style subculture other Asian crews now copy.

name: PRRC 1936 (Private Road Running Club)
who: Seoul's OG run crew of designers, DJs and architects; group runs plus member-designed technical gear.
why: Widely cited as Asia's most influential run crew, the reference point every regional crew that followed name-checks.

name: RunnersHai
who: Shanghai's longest-running social run club; free weekly West Bund sessions with a certified coach plus race meetups.
why: The steady anchor of Shanghai's running scene for over a decade; its real community lives on WeChat more than Instagram.

name: Harbour Runners
who: No-sign-up Wednesday night run crew that has explored Hong Kong on foot since 2010.
why: Started as a stress reliever for creative professionals, grew into Hong Kong's most recognized grassroots running community.

name: Singapore Runners Club
who: Singapore's largest general running club; weekly social runs and relay events across the island.
why: The default landing spot for anyone in Singapore looking for a running community to join.

name: IndoRunners
who: Indonesia's biggest running community; Sunday morning and Thursday night group runs in Jakarta plus chapters nationwide.
why: With tens of thousands of members across platforms, it's the largest and most established run community in Southeast Asia.

name: Rockwell Run Club
who: Makati-based run club with multiple weekly sessions around the Rockwell district for runners of any level.
why: Grew from a handful of runners in 2023 into one of Metro Manila's fastest-growing clubs, now working with hotels on run events.

name: Sabai Run Club
who: Sunday 7:15am mass social run through Bangkok, billed as Asia's largest weekly run club.
why: Turnout in the thousands most Sundays makes it the biggest single recurring run session in the region.

name: Mumbai Road Runners
who: Mumbai's long-running road-running community; weekly group runs and training support for members of any level.
why: One of India's oldest running clubs, casual and community-oriented rather than results-driven.

name: Delhi Run Collective
who: Membership-based Delhi run club with structured weekly sessions across the city.
why: Built a more curated, retention-focused running community in a city where most groups are informal chat threads.

name: Urban Swaras Running Club
who: Nairobi's premier recreational running club; Saturday 7am trail runs at rotating locations since 2006.
why: Two decades of steady Saturday trail runs made it the default community for recreational, non-elite runners in Nairobi.

name: Eko Runners Club
who: Lagos running community with regular group runs and health-focused meetups across the mainland.
why: One of the more visible grassroots crews in a city where organized running culture is still young.

name: Gugulethu Athletics Club
who: Official Western Cape athletics club based in the township of Gugulethu, training runners of all levels, not just competitive athletes.
why: A genuine community institution known for its annual reconciliation race and for building running culture where infrastructure is scarce.

name: Ghetto Run Crew (Movimento Ghetto Run Crew)
who: Zona Norte Rio running collective; free bi-weekly runs from Engenhão stadium, open to all levels.
why: Grew out of a women's-empowerment project into one of Rio's most recognized grassroots crews, built on access over pace.

name: City Runners
who: Nike-supported São Paulo run crew with weekly group training and city meetups.
why: One of the biggest, best-known crew brands in São Paulo's running scene, with real turnout behind the Nike backing.

name: MNKS Run Crew
who: Mexico City run crew ('Monkeys') with weekly group runs and long-run training since 2017.
why: Grew from three founders into a 40-plus-member fixture of CDMX's running scene.

name: CorrerAyuda
who: Palermo-based running team combining group training with charity fundraising runs.
why: Built a loyal following by pairing serious training culture with a give-back mission distinct in Buenos Aires' scene.

name: Unofficial Run Club
who: North Sydney's massive free run-and-pastries club; multiple weekly meetups drawing hundreds of runners.
why: Grew from a small group into Australia's biggest run club in under two years, driving the country's run-club boom.

name: Melbourne Runners
who: Melbourne's largest general running community since 2016; weekly social group runs across the city.
why: The long-running default running community for Melbourne, less trend-driven than newer crews but consistently strong.
